title: In space, blood in your neck can run backward 🩸
subject: astronaut
description:
Would you still go to the space station after this? 👇

A 2019 study of 11 International Space Station astronauts found stalled or reversed blood flow in the jugular vein in 6 of them, and a clot in one. Here's what zero gravity does to the blood in your neck.

Sources: Marshall-Goebel K. et al., "Assessment of Jugular Venous Blood Flow Stasis and Thrombosis During Spaceflight," JAMA Network Open 2019;2(11):e1915011; Phys.org, "Spaceflight can make blood flow the wrong way" (Nov 19, 2019).
tags: what space does to your body

scenes.text: In space, the blood in your neck can flow backward.
Without gravity, fluid in your body drifts toward your head.
In a 2019 study, 11 astronauts on the International Space Station scanned their own necks with ultrasound.
Around day 50, 6 of them had blood in the jugular vein that stalled or ran the wrong way.
Pressure in that vein quadrupled. One astronaut had a clot blocking it completely.
The paper in JAMA Network Open called it a newly discovered risk of spaceflight.
